To paraphrase Super Bowl LXI halftime show headliner Jay Z , the NFL may or may not have 99 problems but a new trial over the long alleged and much litigated Sunday Ticket antitrust violation is now one.
Not that the Roger Goodell -led league are taking this new play on the chin.
“We are disappointed by today’s decision in the NFL Sunday Ticket appeal, the latest development in this case which has been ongoing now for over 11 years – and now promises to go on even longer,” an NFL spokesperson told Deadline soon after the new ruling came down. A panel for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit wrote today: “We conclude that the district court abused its discretion by excluding the subscriber’s expert testimony.” This revives the case the NFL hoped was dead and perviously saw a hardcore $4.7 billion verdict against the leagure a couple of years ago. Watch on Deadline
“By inquiring beyond the reliability of the expert’s method and the sufficiency of their data, the district court exceeded its gatekeeping role under Federal Rule of Evidence 702,” Judge Anthony Johnstone wrote in a 64-page opinion. “But the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding that the jury improperly considered the expert testimony in its damages award. Because the judgment rested on the Rule 702 exclusions, we reversed that decision, affirmed the new trial order, and remanded instructions to reinstate the jury’s liability verdict and for a new trial on damages.”
Boom! In the end zone! In what could be a very expensive and certainly drawn out end zone for the NFL.
The big flex by the San Francisco-based three-judge appeals court panel comes more than two years after U.S. District Court Judge Philip S. Gutierrez threw aside a jury’s $4.7 billion judgment against the 32-team league over the alleged artificially inflated cost to consumers of its prized NFL Sunday Ticket subscriptions.
Initially filed in 2015, the class action covers 2.4 million residential subscribers and 48,000 businesses such as bars and restaurants who forked out cash for out-of-market games over the 2011 to 2022 NFL seasons on DirecTV . Back in August 2024, Judge Gutierrez ruled the experts who offered testimony and analysis for the class action’s plaintiffs employed flawed economic models.
Today, after the much anticipated and honestly not that surprising result, the NFL was dusting off the old playbook and getting ready to go back on the field in the price-fixing game of sorts.
“We continue to believe that our media distribution strategy – which features 100 percent of NFL games broadcast on free over-the-air television in the markets of the participating teams and national distribution of our most popular games, supplemented by many additional choices including RedZone, Sunday Ticket and NFL Plus – is by far the most fan-friendly distribution model in all of sports and entertainment,” that league spokesperson added. “We appreciate the panel’s attention to this case, and we will be considering our options for seeking further appellate review of today’s decision.”
BTW – if you don’t know, Sunday Ticket isn’t even on DirecTV anymore. As all the litigation was going on, the NFL inked a seven-year, $14 billion deal with YouTube TV in 2023, putting Sunday Ticket on streaming.

नेशनल फुटबॉल लीग (NFL) को अपने 'संडे टिकट' एंटीट्रस्ट मुकदमे के संबंध में एक नए मुकदमे का सामना करना पड़ रहा है, क्योंकि एक संघीय अपीलीय अदालत के फैसले ने इस लंबे समय से चले आ रहे कानूनी विवाद को फिर से जिंदा कर दिया है।

NFL के एक प्रवक्ता ने कहा कि लीग इस फैसले से निराश है और आगे की अपीलीय समीक्षा के लिए अपने विकल्पों पर विचार कर रही है। इससे पहले, इस मामले में एक जूरी ने भारी-भरकम फैसले की घोषणा की थी, जिसे बाद में एक जिला अदालत के जज ने यह कहते हुए खारिज कर दिया था कि वादी के विशेषज्ञ की गवाही त्रुटिपूर्ण आर्थिक मॉडल पर आधारित थी।

## अपीलीय अदालत का फैसला

यू.एस. कोर्ट ऑफ अपील्स फॉर द नाइंथ सर्किट के एक पैनल ने निष्कर्ष निकाला कि जिला अदालत ने सब्सक्राइबर के विशेषज्ञ की गवाही को बाहर करके अपने विवेक का दुरुपयोग किया था। जज एंथनी जॉनस्टोन ने 64 पेज के अपने फैसले में लिखा कि निचली अदालत ने फेडरल रूल ऑफ एविडेंस 702 के तहत अपनी भूमिका की सीमा लांघ दी थी। हालांकि, अपीलीय पैनल ने यह भी माना कि जूरी द्वारा हर्जाने के फैसले में गवाही पर विचार करने के तरीके में जिला अदालत ने कोई अनुचित त्रुटि नहीं पाई। परिणामस्वरूप, पैनल ने पिछले फैसले को पलट दिया, नए मुकदमे के आदेश को बरकरार रखा, देयता फैसले को बहाल किया और विशेष रूप से हर्जाने पर एक नए मुकदमे के लिए मामले को वापस भेज दिया।

## मुकदमे की पृष्ठभूमि

मूल रूप से 2015 में दायर किए गए इस क्लास-एक्शन मुकदमे में लाखों आवासीय ग्राहक और हजारों व्यवसाय शामिल हैं जिन्होंने कई सत्रों में आउट-ऑफ-मार्केट गेम खरीदे थे। NFL का तर्क है कि इसकी मीडिया वितरण रणनीति प्रशंसकों के अनुकूल बनी हुई है, जिसमें स्थानीय बाजारों में मुफ्त ओवर-द-एयर प्रसारण और अतिरिक्त सदस्यता विकल्प शामिल हैं।

* **मामले की शुरुआत:** 2015 में 2011-2022 सत्रों को कवर करते हुए दायर किया गया।
* **प्रभावित पक्ष:** लगभग 24 लाख आवासीय ग्राहक और 48,000 व्यवसाय।
* **वर्तमान स्थिति:** देयता फैसले को बहाल कर दिया गया है और हर्जाने पर नए मुकदमे का आदेश दिया गया है।

पाठक यू.एस. कोर्ट ऑफ अपील्स फॉर द नाइंथ सर्किट के सार्वजनिक रिकॉर्ड और आधिकारिक लीग बयानों के माध्यम से अदालत के दस्तावेजों की पुष्टि कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
The National Football League is facing a new trial regarding its 'Sunday Ticket' antitrust litigation after a federal appeals court ruling revived the long-running legal battle.

An NFL spokesperson stated that the league is disappointed by the decision and is considering options for further appellate review. Previously, a jury had returned a multi-billion-dollar verdict in the case, which was later set aside by a district court judge who ruled that plaintiffs' expert testimony relied on flawed economic models.

## Appeals Court Decision

A panel for the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit concluded that the district court abused its discretion by excluding subscriber expert testimony. Writing in a 64-page opinion, Judge Anthony Johnstone stated that the lower court exceeded its gatekeeping role under Federal Rule of Evidence 702. However, the appeals panel also found that the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding issues with how the jury considered testimony in its damages award. Consequently, the panel reversed the prior judgment, affirmed a new trial order, reinstated the liability verdict, and remanded the case for a new trial specifically on damages.

## Background of the Litigation

The class-action lawsuit, initially filed in 2015, covers millions of residential subscribers and tens of thousands of businesses that purchased out-of-market games over multiple seasons. The NFL maintains that its media distribution strategy remains fan-friendly, pointing to free over-the-air broadcasts in local markets alongside subscription options.

* **Case Origin:** Filed in 2015 covering 2011–2022 seasons.
* **Affected Parties:** Approximately 2.4 million residential subscribers and 48,000 businesses.
* **Current Status:** The liability verdict was reinstated, and a new trial on damages was ordered.

Readers can verify court filings through the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit public docket records and official league statements.
